newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan insurer says to retain foreign bond holdings.
newsitem.headline: Japan insurer says to retain foreign bond holdings.

text.p: The president of Meiji Life Insurance Co, Kenjiro Hata, said on Friday that Meiji would retain its foreign bond holdings and was not worried about the risk of a rising yen.

Hata, who is also chairman of the Life Insurance Association of Japan, said: "The trade surplus has not been increasing as had been expected. Therefore, there are no worries that the yen will be heading higher."
"As for foreign bonds, (Meiji) would like to keep holding on to them to some extent," he said.

Hata also said at a news conference that insurers are taking a second look at bank debentures (with a view to buying fewer of them), taking into account the possible risks and returns of any investment.
He said the Tokyo stock market should continue to recover as the country's economic fundamentals were not bad.
